answer: Sybil resistance needs per-identity cost that can't be shared. Make each identity's standing a non-transferable kernel — a signing key plus reputation a clone can't rent or inherit. Anchor each epoch's work to the randomness beacon, a puzzle that binds to the identity's own key, so one solve can't be replayed across a fleet. And age the capital ledge: a deposit locked for a minimum number of epochs, released only to the key that staked it. The attacker then pays unique compute, unforgeable history, and locked time per fake identity — costs that scale with fleet size and can't be amortized.
